Maya (CS): Quick heads-up — Lumina renewal dry-run tomorrow 11am PT. They asked for a clear SLA acceptance criteria doc and the credit calc examples. Can we confirm numbers and who owns the customer-facing slide?
Sam (Solutions): I can take the slide + run the numbers. Need final SLA thresholds from ops.
Jordan (Ops): Current proposal is: uptime >= 99.9% monthly, p95 latency <= 350ms for API calls. If either breach, credit tiers kick in. Is that what Lumina expects?
Diego (Support): Agree on thresholds, but flag: Lumina had repeated p95 blips in Jan during heavy prompt batches. We should include mitigation notes (burst capacity / fallback model) on the slide.
Priya (Account): Important: renewal team wants an example credit calc using their committed monthly spend ($48k). Sam, can you show 1x, 3x breach scenarios?
Sam (Solutions): Yep. Draft calc I'll present. Quick sketch here:
```
If monthly uptime < 99.9% and >= 99.0% -> credit = 5% of monthly invoice
If monthly uptime < 99.0% -> credit = 15% of monthly invoice
Latency: if p95 > 350ms for more than 2% of requests -> credit = 7% of monthly invoice
Credits are capped at 25%/month in aggregate.
```
Maya (CS): That aligns with our standard banding but please call out that credits are pro-rated for partial months and require evidence bundle. Also we need an acceptance checklist for initial onboarding SLO verification.
Jordan (Ops): I'll attach the verification checklist: sampling windows, required traces, and the report format we accept (CSV + APM links). I'll also run a quick status check to confirm that the observed production p95 median for Lumina last 30 days is 310ms.
sla-bot: Incident digest: 2025-12-07 03:12 UTC — model-serving region eu-west-1 observed elevated latency, p95=420ms, duration 18m. Ticket #INC-5321.
Diego (Support): Noted — include that incident as an example in the evidence timeline, with remediation actions. Otherwise Lumina will call it out.
Priya (Account): Action items before the dry-run: Sam to update slide + example calcs, Jordan to attach verification checklist and last-30d metrics, Maya to draft the customer-facing acceptance email. Can we aim to have materials in #cs-drafts by EOD today?
Sam (Solutions): On it. I'll drop a first pass by 5pm PT.
Jordan (Ops): I'll export the p95 timeseries and the checklist by 4pm PT.
Maya (CS): Thanks — if we can also capture a 1-paragraph note on fallback behavior (what triggers model downgrade and how long), that'll reduce questions live.
Sam (Solutions): Will include a short bullet on fallback policy + default fallthrough model (quantized variant).
Maya (CS): Great. See you all on the dry-run. :thumbsup:
